rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate all six peaks and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The elution window will guide gradient trimming and subsequent slope and temperature tests.

Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF, so retain it as the benchmark. Shortening only tG tests whether the run can be accelerated while preserving full resolution, using the minimum R of 3.78 as headroom.

Both runs attained the maximum CRF, but the shorter gradient leaves the critical pair near the resolution threshold. Raising temperature alone tests whether selectivity permits a faster fully resolved run; injection 2 remains the faster validated benchmark.

Shorten the gradient by one grid step at 50 C to test the speed limit while holding temperature selectivity constant. Injection 3 remains a validated maximum-CRF fallback if the critical pair drops below R = 1.5.

Reduce gradient steepness by lowering phi1 while retaining the shorter tG; the last peak previously eluted near phi = 0.53, leaving ample endpoint headroom. This should recover critical-pair resolution and target a faster maximum-CRF method than injection 3.

Raise phi0 one step to reduce early retention while slightly flattening the gradient, which may preserve the slope-sensitive critical pair. This tests a faster fully resolved method against injection 5, which already achieves maximum CRF.

Increase phi0 to further shorten retention while flattening the gradient to protect the critical middle pair. Monitor the first two peaks for compression as initial solvent strength rises; injection 6 remains a fully resolved fallback.

Raise phi0 by one grid step to seek another reduction in elution time while retaining a shallow gradient for the critical middle pair. Check early-pair resolution carefully because the first peak is approaching the unretained region.

Lower phi1 one step to flatten the gradient and recover the small resolution deficit in the middle pair. The last peak eluted near phi = 0.49, so this endpoint retains ample elution strength and may yield full resolution faster than injection 7.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a much steeper gradient for a faster alternative where the critical middle pair may separate again after an elution-order reversal. Lower phi0 than injection 9 provides more retention for the early pair during this exploratory run.

Test temperature selectivity at the fast gradient while holding the solvent program fixed. Cooling should improve early retention and may separate the nearly co-eluting middle pair; injection 9 remains the fastest validated maximum-CRF method.

Raise phi0 to test whether the stronger starting solvent improves selectivity of the unresolved middle pair on the fast, low-temperature branch. Injection 11 has ample early-pair resolution, but both the middle and final pairs need monitoring.

Test a stronger starting solvent on the fast, low-temperature branch to see whether initial-solvent selectivity can separate the persistent middle pair. The early pair has resolution headroom, but monitor it closely for compression toward the dead time.

Test a steeper gradient at the same starting composition and temperature to determine whether the fast-branch middle pair gains resolution after its apparent order reversal. Keep phi0 fixed because the first peak is already essentially unretained.

The steeper gradient reduced middle-pair resolution, so test a substantially shallower slope at the same phi0 and temperature. The last peak previously eluted near phi = 0.53, making this endpoint a reasonable test for recovering full resolution with a short gradient and final hold.

Return to the fully resolved selectivity of injection 9 and shorten the programmed gradient while keeping its slope nearly unchanged. The slightly steeper slope targets a modestly faster maximum-CRF method, with phi1 still above the observed elution window.

Test a one-step temperature decrease around the fastest fully resolved method to measure local selectivity changes at the trimmed solvent window. This will show whether cooling creates resolution headroom for further gradient acceleration; injection 16 remains the maximum-CRF fallback.

Use the starting composition of injection 7 with a moderately steeper gradient to approach its resolution limit and shorten elution time. This tests whether the lower phi0 offers enough middle-pair selectivity to match or improve injection 16 while preserving full early-pair resolution.

Test a gradient slope between fully resolved injection 7 and marginally unresolved injection 18. This should recover full middle-pair resolution while retaining most of the time savings from the steeper gradient.

Test one final starting-solvent step on the fast, low-temperature branch, where increasing phi0 previously improved the critical middle pair. This deliberately probes the tradeoff against early-pair compression; injection 16 remains the fastest validated maximum-CRF fallback.

Raise temperature one step from the fastest fully resolved method to test whether improved middle-pair selectivity permits a shorter elution time. Monitor the early pair closely, since its resolution decreased with temperature in the scouting runs; injection 16 remains the validated fallback.

Lower phi0 one step to restore early-pair retention at 55 C while keeping the endpoint and gradient duration fixed. This tests whether the higher-temperature method can recover full resolution; injection 16 remains the fastest validated maximum-CRF method.

Return to 50 C and flatten the gradient one step from injection 16 to increase the narrow middle-pair resolution margin. Maximum CRF is already secured, so this refinement targets a short method with more resolution headroom rather than further temperature-driven compression.

Trim injection 7's gradient duration and endpoint while preserving its validated slope and temperature. All peaks should elute before the gradient ends, targeting the same maximum CRF and resolution margin with a shorter programmed gradient.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower gradient for additional middle-pair resolution while preserving early retention and a short run. Maximum CRF is already achieved; injection 16 remains the fastest validated fully resolved method at t_last = 3.40 min.
